question_or_symptom: A memory request can mutate remote state before its ACK is validated while queue completions from earlier acknowledged work may legitimately arrive first.
observation: Retrying an ambiguous ALLOC, FREE, H2D, or D2H request can duplicate or reverse mutation. Rejecting every interleaved queue completion breaks a valid shared session, while accepting an uncorrelated or current-request completion hides protocol drift.
conclusion: Session reuse depends on a precise distinction between determinate remote outcomes, indeterminate request outcomes, and local post-ACK completion work.
decision: Share one strictly increasing request-ID sequence across queue and memory records; buffer only canonical completions for previously ACKed pending queue commands; keep canonical non-OK memory ACKs reusable; poison on any complete-send timeout, cancellation, EOF, identity, shape, carrier, or CRC ambiguity before canonical ACK; and allow a successful D2H ACK followed only by local deadline or cancellation to preserve output and session for explicit FREE.
invalidated_assumptions: Every timeout can be retried on the same session because the operation is synchronous.
Any queue completion may be buffered while a memory ACK is outstanding.
